Missing `check_changed_settings_in_group()`.
Useless check.
`is_dragging_dock` is always true here, no?

```suggestion
	Ref<InputEventMouseMotion> me = p_event;
```
Other events aren't really relevant.

```suggestion
				if (from_node && Object::cast_to<EditorDockTabContainer>(from_node->get_parent())) {
```
Also it would be nice to avoid casting twice. You can utilize early return for that.
But why is this not inside `input()`, where `mouse_inside` is set?
EditorDockTabContainer is still a TabContainer, so these changes should be unnecessary.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106762/files#r2110295167

EditorDockTabContainer's logic is entirely internal, so you can use TabContainer.
Where is this needed?

Because the mouse cursor is set inside `gui_input()` (specifically `viewport::_gui_input_event()`), and `input()` is called before that, so any changes to the cursor shape will be overridden by the viewport. The only reason to have this is to have the proper cursor shape.
You could use `call_deferred()` for that.
I'll give that a try

```suggestion
```
Already forward declared
Instead of using drop_data, this should use EditorDockManager::_move_dock, since drop_data should only be called by Viewport.

For all of this, I wanted to simplify the SplitContainers first so the logic for this can be much simpler, more dynamic, and not rely on hard coded dock slots. I got stalled working on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90411 for this, I guess I need to get back to working on it.
Also I think these can overlap and be sorted so some have more priority, to simplify it.
For now it might be best to only cover the open dock slots like before, and the closed dock slots can be done later.

This can just cover the contents, so the TabContainer drag and drop logic works the same as before, and dropping it on the contents just adds it to the end.
`dock_slot[i]->get_current_tab_control()->get_global_rect();`.

And this logic to set the rects should be from EditorDockManager's drag begin notification, so it only happens once instead of for each one.
I'll limit it to visible slots then.

Unfortunately since `EditorDockManager` is an Object and not in the tree, it does not receive the drag notification. However, I already have safeguards against computing the information multiple times, it stores the output and has an early return if the output is already known for the current drag.

Although if I limit the drop rect to the child control, then the highlight won't appear when the mouse is over the tabbar unless I returned to using `input()`. What do you think about this?

If it doesn't get the notification, then it is fine. In the future we may want to move some dock management into a Control.

I think it's fine to not highlight when the mouse is over the TabBar, since it has its own drop highlight and it allows moving the tab to a different index.

Actually thinking about it, I do think that we should override the TabBar drag and dropping. If we want to limit where the dock can be dropped (ie for different horizontal / vertical layouts), we need to change the behavior somewhat, and I think that this is the place. I might try and see if I can somehow update the TabBar's drop hint.

Dropping the tab on a dock should move it to the end by default, currently it never puts it at the end. 
I think only when the tab is over the TabBar part should you be able to change the index.

I'm still not sure why the TabBar needs to be covered. For moving to closed slots in the future, it can either be on top of the TabBars or work around it, since dropping directly into the TabBar should probably always drop into the TabBar.
If it is needed for some reason, then the TabBar's tab drag index highlight should be recreated so you know what index the dock will be at when dropped.

```suggestion
```
This isn't really needed.
Maybe this should draw a partially transparent center so it is more clear that it isn't for the dock's content?

I've recreated the tab drag index highlight by copying the code from `tab_bar.cpp`, and am calling the TabBar's public `_handle_drop_data` function in order to actually drop the dock. I could copy that logic as well but I felt that it would be best to not duplicate code as much as possible.

I do think that the TabBar should be covered because if we want to limit vertical docks from being dragged into horizontal areas, we will need to override the behavior of the TabBar's drag and drop, and since this control already needs to override the drag and drop in order to drop in the whole area, I do think that it is the place.

is_layout_horizontal is always false, so this check doesn't do anything and invalid color is never used, even after #106503. 
We can just set can_drop_dock to true, and remove the invalid color for now. When a PR adds horizontal slots it can be re-added then, if it is wanted.
I removed the two variables, so its a bit cleaner now.
Can be early return.
`can_drop_data()` already ensures this.
